summary:
**ORBITERRA ATLAS – From Space to the Soil**

ORBITERRA ATLAS is an Earth observation and agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It focuses on the Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka, India, bringing Earth data, climate information and crop-water scenario analysis into one workspace.

The platform includes an interactive dashboard for exploring environmental conditions, a Crop Resilience & Scenario Lab for comparing crop water requirements, and an ORBITERRA AI section for agricultural decision support. Its scenario modelling allows users to examine how rainfall, evapotranspiration, soil-water storage, crop coefficients and irrigation influence the soil-water balance.

ORBITERRA ATLAS addresses the challenge by making Earth and climate information easier to understand and explore in an agricultural context. It is important because changing rainfall patterns and limited water availability make crop planning increasingly difficult. By helping users explore crop-water scenarios and understand environmental conditions, the platform aims to support more informed and climate-resilient agricultural decisions.
details:
ORBITERRA ATLAS – From Space to the Soil

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

ORBITERRA ATLAS is an Earth observation and agricultural decision-support platform designed for the Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka, India. It brings environmental information, climate conditions and crop-water scenario analysis into one digital workspace.

The application has five main navigation areas: Home, Dashboard, Crop Resilience Analysis, ORBITERRA AI, and Data & Methodology.

The Dashboard provides an overview of environmental conditions and satellite-informed soil-moisture estimates. The Crop Resilience & Scenario Lab allows users to explore different crop-water scenarios by adjusting parameters such as initial soil-water storage, soil-water capacity, rainfall, reference evapotranspiration, crop coefficients, irrigation and scenario duration.

The model uses these inputs to explore how water availability changes under different conditions, helping users understand potential agricultural challenges.

2. What are the benefits?

  • Brings Earth observation, climate and agricultural information together.
  • Helps users understand crop-water requirements.
  • Allows comparison of different rainfall and irrigation scenarios.
  • Makes environmental and agricultural concepts easier to explore.
  • Encourages informed water-management and crop-planning decisions.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our aim is to support more climate-resilient agriculture by making environmental information understandable and useful for agricultural planning. ORBITERRA ATLAS can help farmers, students and agricultural researchers explore how changing rainfall and water availability may affect crop decisions.

In the future, the platform can be expanded with locally validated agricultural information and stronger decision-support capabilities.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

  • Programming language: Python.
  • Application framework: Streamlit.
  • Deployment: Streamlit Community Cloud.
  • Software: Visual Studio Code and web-based development tools.
  • Application components: Interactive dashboards, user-adjustable scenario inputs, charts and analytical visualisations.
  • Hardware: A standard computer and internet connection for development and access.

No specialised agricultural hardware or field sensors are required for the current software prototype.

5. What makes the project creative?

The creative aspect of ORBITERRA ATLAS is its approach of connecting information from Earth observation and climate science with a practical crop-water scenario explorer.

Instead of simply displaying environmental information, the platform allows users to experiment with different conditions and understand how rainfall, evapotranspiration, soil-water storage and irrigation influence agricultural water availability.

Its central concept is to translate complex environmental information into an accessible agricultural decision-support experience.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The project focuses on the Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka and considers:

  • Regional climate and rainfall variability.
  • Soil-water storage and water-holding capacity.
  • Crop water requirements and crop coefficients.
  • Reference evapotranspiration.
  • Irrigation availability and water-management scenarios.
  • The importance of clear data sources and transparent assumptions.
  • The need for local agricultural validation before using model outputs for actual farm decisions.

The current Crop Resilience Lab clearly identifies its default rainfall, evapotranspiration and crop-coefficient profiles as illustrative inputs rather than verified local farm observations.

ORBITERRA ATLAS aims to turn Earth data into understandable agricultural insights and encourage smarter, more resilient crop-water planning.
